The edges C–D and D–E are in the accent color: each is the only link between its two sides, so removing it disconnects the graph. The card lists the bridges C–D and D–E." width="100%"} A bridge (also called a cut edge) is an edge whose removal increases the number of connected components. Bridges are critical edges that, if removed, would disconnect parts of the network. Uses Tarjan's algorithm for undirected graphs (`O(V + E)` time complexity) and strongly connected component analysis for directed graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge IDs that are bridges. Empty list if no bridges exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Bridge detection uses Tarjan's DFS-based algorithm on undirected graphs, which finds every bridge in $O(V + E)$ by tracking each node's DFS entry time and the lowest such time reachable from its subtree; an edge $(u, v)$ is a bridge iff no back edge from $v$'s subtree reaches $u$ or an earlier ancestor. On directed graphs the notion generalizes to strongly-connected-component analysis, since removing an edge that connects two SCCs severs any cross-component paths. Every edge of a tree is a bridge; a cycle contains none. Bridges are the edge-level analogue of `articulation_points()`, and together the two identify a graph's most fragile choke points. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path graph has no cycles, so removing any single edge splits it in two — every edge is a bridge: ::: {#82de8588 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(4) bridges = graph.bridges() # Returns 3 (all edges are bridges in a path) len(bridges) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Attaching a "tail" node to an otherwise cyclic graph creates exactly one bridge: the edge connecting the tail to the cycle, since the cycle itself has no bridges: ::: {#788cf28c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(4) # 0-1-2-3-0 graph.add_node(label="tail") tail_id = graph.get_id_from_label("tail") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.add_edge(nodes[-1], tail_id) # Add a tail bridges = graph.bridges() # Returns 1 (only the edge to the tail is a bridge) len(bridges) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: The returned IDs can be resolved back to node pairs to see exactly which connections are critical: ::: {#618e34c5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(3) bridge_ids = graph.bridges() # Each bridge maps back to a (source, target) node pair [graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(eid) for eid in bridge_ids] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [(1, 2), (2, 3)] ``` ::: :::
